newsitem.title: USA: Tax reform bill fails in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Tax reform bill fails in Texas.

text.p: A proposed tax cut viewed as a stepping stone for a possible presidential campaign by Texas Gov. George W. Bush died Saturday in the Texas Legislature.

The bill, which Bush hoped would cut property taxes by up to 40 percent, failed when the Texas House of Representatives and Senate could not come up with a compromise on how much to reduce taxes and how best to pay for them.

The proposal put forth by Bush in January would have reduced taxes for homeowners, but included new taxes on business to help fund school districts. The idea of a new business tax ran into stiff opposition from various sectors in the state's business establishment, which ultimately helped kill the proposal with a powerful lobbying effort.
"There is no question that it is hard in some cases to convince people who don't pay taxes to pay taxes for the good of schoolchildren," Bush told reporters when it was clear the cut was dead.

The Texas House and Senate, who are nearing the end of their current session, passed separate, widely different tax cut bills earlier this spring. Intense negotiations this week failed to come up a with a single, compromise bill to present to both chambers.
On Saturday, negotiators from the House and Senate declared current tax relief efforts dead. The Texas Legislature is not scheduled to meet again until 1999.

"One of these days, the legislature of this state will step up to the plate and do what it needs to do. Unfortunately, it's not today," said State Representative Paul Sadler, who was on the negotiating committee.

Bush's proposal was seen as a first step toward a possible run for the presidency in 2000. Political experts said that by passing a big tax cut he would be a top candidate to win the Republican presidential nomination.

Bush, whose father is former President George Bush, has denied the tax cut proposal was aimed at positioning for a presidential run, but has not ruled out the possibility of making a bid for the nation's highest office.
